threshold_change_policy: Frozen before model implementation and acceptance executions; diagnostic controls are not passes. Any correction requires source/specification evidence and adversarial review, never pass-outcome tuning.
global_requirements: Ordinary launches use the official mask ROM and strict file-backed NOR segments. Extract exactly 16 KiB from the Pico1 B2 ROM. Do not seed ELF BSS, heap, or USB DPRAM; patch CPU PC/SP/VTOR/security state; or recognize examples in models.

Keep example, SDK, and FreeRTOS sources pinned and unchanged except for explicit reviewed exceptions. Official picotool postlink bi_ptr configuration is a designed data fixture. Preserve original/configured ELF and UF2 hashes, instruction identity, data diffs, and matching NOR payloads.

Record managed/native build provenance, actual per-core loaded module hashes, helper/wrapper/Renode terminal statuses, raw GPIO/UART/IRQ/address/register events, and source/input/configuration hashes. Diagnostic-only runs are not passes.
Reject unexpected panic, assertion, fault, or lockup. The original FreeRTOS task-return defect control is negative evidence only. Finite examples must actually exit with status zero.
Use virtual time for timing checks without changing firmware delays, sample counts, or tick rates. Observers must preserve bus values and never fabricate effects.

USB checks require an isolated Linux guest, an exclusive exchange lease, actual descriptors/control/bulk and CDC/MSC behavior, and clean import detachment. Coordinate any physical fixture use with root; this milestone uses emulation.
Propagate private HOME/XDG/TMP/Cargo/NuGet/dotnet paths to subprocesses. Preserve failed, interrupted, and setup attempts separately from selected successful cases.

Keep the existing 32 Pico cases, affected model/platform suites, and original three Metalclaw smokes passing. Require a fresh independent source build and all 32 new cases with the same frozen inputs and criteria. Do not claim all 274 examples, the custom board, or Quasar are complete.

Commit incrementally in repository style without AI attribution. Do not push without current-message authorization. Clean owned processes and local worker refs as work finishes, while preserving user changes, generated files, and frozen runtime dependencies; archive branch history before audited pruning.

Boot through the actual ROM from a cold machine. The pre-main constructor must complete its nominal 200 ms flag window, followed by at least three complete GPIO25 blink cycles.

Start from normal main execution. The first actual RUN assertion/release starts a new pre-main window. A second RUN assertion/release 100 ms after constructor entry must detect the retained token and enter the official ROM BOOTSEL path before main reenters. Two explicit RUN pulses 300 ms apart must let the first window expire. The subsequent boot must reach main and blink rather than enter BOOTSEL. Record reset edges and ROM, constructor, and main timestamps.

Pico1 must retain ordinary SRAM, including the SDK noinit flag, across RUN. Preserve upstream tick rate 1000 Hz, LED_BUSY_WAIT=1, USE_LED=1, and priorities main=2, blink=1, worker=4. The one-core target runs on core0; two-core and static-allocation targets use SMP2 with main affinity mask 1. The static target must use static allocation with dynamic allocation disabled and actual static TCB/stack storage; dynamic targets use Heap4. Record effective definitions and link maps. Do not change core counts, priorities, or timing to bypass failures.

Observe exactly main counts 0..9 in order, separated by 3000 ticks/about three seconds, then "main_task is exiting now" and completed async_context_deinit. Do not stop before 30 seconds or accept a startup banner alone. After any reviewed lifecycle repair, require actual task deletion and continued progress from other tasks.

Observe actual do_work thread callbacks with counts 0, 1, and 2 at about 0, 10, and 20 seconds. Count 3 near 30 seconds is allowed only before deinitialization. Require no callbacks after deinitialization, including at least 11 virtual seconds of post-completion observation. Do not lose, duplicate, or synthesize counts.

GPIO25 must alternate low/high at two-second intervals while main blocks and the worker preempts, then continue after main finishes and deletes its task. The initial false level is startup, not a complete cycle.

Observe actual SysTick/PendSV entries and context switches, with task callbacks in thread mode. One-core tasks must run only on core0. In SMP builds, both native cores must execute FreeRTOS task contexts, while main remains on core0 and worker/blink may run on either core. Do not demand migration or an unspecified fixed worker core.

Preserve an original runtime/ELF/disassembly control through that point. No patch is authorized yet. If confirmed unavoidable, a minimal vTaskDelete(NULL) after deinitialization may be reviewed. Positive acceptance requires proper task deletion and subsequent scheduling, never a panic allowance or early stop.
